non_song.why: Al's between-song announcements. Tapers write it "al.nouncements", "Al.nouncments" and "al.nouncement" -- matching "nounc" catches the lot, where matching "unceme" would miss the spelling with no 'e' after the 'c'.

"Alnowncements". The "nounc" spelling was chosen to catch every way a taper writes Al's announcements, and this one still got past it: squashed it reads "alnowncements", with a 'w' where the 'u' belongs. It sat in the vocabulary as a song with n=1 and a median of 85 seconds.

Not a moe. song. It is a hype MC introducing the band, and he does it with very consistent timing -- which is exactly what makes it dangerous: it looks like a tight, reliable 90-second opener and a length model would believe it.
Between-song stage talk, never a titled performance. Free-floating so it also catches "Crowd Banter" and "Break/Banter".

"Greeting By Al" -- Al saying hello to the room. This lived in setlistkit's generic junk filter, which DROPS, and that was the wrong side of the line: a greeting happened on the stage and is not music, which makes it a tag. Dropped, the corpus lost the fact that the band opened by talking. Free-floating so it also catches "Greetings" and "Al's Greeting"; checked against all 306 squashed titles for an accidental cross-word match ("The Ogre Eating" squashes to theogreeating, not theogreeting) and there is none.
Stage business, not a song: "adjustments & comments", "comments & calling up Andy".
Gear business. Spelled out in full rather than reaching for a pattern like "amp$", which would take Vamp and anything else ending that way with it.
moe.day is the band's own festival and a "moe.day Proclamation" is Al reading it out, not a song.
A note the description parser mistook for a song.

The setlist sometimes labels a reprise outright -- "Moth (reprise)". Take it at its word: a reprise is real music but it is not a performance of the song, and it drags the median down exactly like the unlabelled ones we catch by ear.
